greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Grace and peace be with you all as we gather in prayer.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the strength of our lives and the anchor of our hope. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you know every ache of our hearts and you carry our burdens. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you lead us safely home to the eternal banquet of the Father. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
homily:
We begin today with something very small and very bright: a window seat on a commercial jet, pressed against the cold glass, looking out over a vast ocean of clouds. Think of what it is like to sit there. The engines hum beneath you, steady and deep. The world below is hidden beneath a blanket of white, and you are suspended between earth and sky, moving toward a destination you cannot yet see, trusting the pilot at the controls. For Benjamin Vo, that view was not just a pastime; it was a passion. Whether he was talking about the engineering of a Boeing 737, imagining his own airline called 'con chim airlines' with a joyful giggle, or studying the complex architecture of cloud infrastructure with his dad, Ben loved the horizon. He loved things that climbed into the sky. He understood that looking up is something we do when our hearts are reaching for something larger than ourselves.

I want you to hold onto that image: the window seat looking out over the clouds. It is the image of a journey—the quiet, focused gaze of someone who knows there is a vast, beautiful world beyond the room we are sitting in right now.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and everyone who holds the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: it has been four months since he went home to God. We know what it is like to walk past a closed bedroom door, to hear the sudden quiet in a house that used to hum with the brilliant mind of a fifteen-year-old boy who was already tackling advanced math and coding his own games. We know the weight of the silence. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary Tuesday. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. 

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side. Illness and sorrow in this fragile world sometimes come completely outside of human control, touching lives without reason or fault. You are not to blame. God does not accuse you, and you must not accuse yourselves. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Listen to what Jesus says to His disciples today in Luke’s Gospel: 'The person who is trustworthy in very small matters is also trustworthy in great ones... If, therefore, you are not trustworthy with dishonest wealth, who will trust you with true wealth?' Jesus is talking about trust, about stewardship, about the small, everyday choices we make with what has been lent to us. But look deeper. Look at the way a young life, even one that feels cut short, is a faithful stewardship of God’s grace. Ben spent his fifteen years being trustworthy in the small matters of love—listening to his dad's stories with total fascination, laughing easily, and caring for others with a tenderness that surprised the world. Think of that remarkable moment when he unprompted told his parents that he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William, who was suffering from strokes. He didn't need to break it open; the offer itself revealed the magnificent generosity of his soul. He was a boy whose heart was already sized for heaven.

Think also of the first reading, from St. Paul to the Philippians. Paul writes from a place of trial, yet he says something astonishing: 'I have learned, in whatever situation I find myself, to be self-sufficient... I have the strength for everything through him who empowers me.' Paul is talking about an inner anchor that does not shift when circumstances change. He speaks of the Philippians' kindness as 'a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.' When we think of Benjamin—his brilliant mind, his bright braces-filled smile in front of a lake, his gentle, respectful spirit—we see that same fragrance. His life was a gift offered back to the Creator. And Paul finishes with a promise that belongs to you today: 'My God will fully supply whatever you need, in accord with his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.' Not in accord with our fears, but in accord with His glorious riches. God is supplying your strength right now, today, in this very hour, even when you feel empty.

Alan, I know how the mind and the heart search for him in the quiet hours. I remember the dream you shared—that bright afternoon when you and Ben were waiting in line to buy ice cream, and Ben stepped up and paid. That wasn't just a random dream; it was a window into the reality of grace. It was Ben telling you what he has discovered on the other side: that he is well, that he is strong, that the roles have shifted only enough for him to care for you now. Just as he said in that other vivid dream: 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết. Con tự thở được bình thường mà... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' He has passed the test. He is breathing the free, clear air of eternity. He is waiting in the light, watching over his mom, his dad, and his best friend.

Ryan, you are carrying a holy, unique weight as his brother. You know the roller coaster rides, the shared laughter, the quiet moments that no one else saw. You are not just the one who remains; you are the one who carries the story forward. When you think of the future, remember that you do not walk alone. Your brother’s love is woven into your courage. Keep being the boy who reaches out, keep living with that same resilient spirit, and know that you are part of a family of four that nothing—not even death—can divide.

To everyone listening from afar—to other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and to every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted.

So what do you carry out the door today? Not a heavy theological puzzle, but one small, doable thing: the next time the house is too quiet and the grief feels too tall to climb, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, cheeky grin with his sunglasses on his head, looking out toward an endless horizon. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity, holding the key. Amen.
petitions: For Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ's peace,
For Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all who mourn the loss of someone dearly loved, that God grant them profound consolation, gentle strength, and an unshakeable hope,
For all children who suffer in body or spirit, and for the families who care for them with tired hands and brave hearts, that they may feel the healing presence of the Lord,
For doctors, researchers, and caregivers working tirelessly to bring healing and cures to the sick, that their efforts be blessed with success,
For our community gathered here today, that we may learn to love generously, live faithfully, and support one another in times of trial,
standing_petitions: For a boy named Ben and all who have died, that they rest in the light of Christ.
For all who grieve, that God console them and give them hope.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot now receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, wipe away every tear from your eyes, and bring you safely home to His eternal peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
I rejoice greatly in the Lord
that now at last you revived your concern for me.
You were, of course, concerned about me but lacked an opportunity.
Not that I say this because of need,
for I have learned, in whatever situation I find myself,
to be self-sufficient.
I know indeed how to live in humble circumstances;
I know also how to live with abundance.
In every circumstance and in all things
I have learned the secret of being well fed and of going hungry,
of living in abundance and of being in need.
I have the strength for everything through him who empowers me.
Still, it was kind of you to share in my distress.You Philippians indeed know that at the beginning of the Gospel,
when I left Macedonia,
not a single church shared with me
in an account of giving and receiving, except you alone.
For even when I was at Thessalonica
you sent me something for my needs,
not only once but more than once.
It is not that I am eager for the gift;
rather, I am eager for the profit that accrues to your account.
I have received full payment and I abound.
I am very well supplied because of what I received from you
through Epaphroditus,
“a fragrant aroma,” an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
My God will fully supply whatever you need,
in accord with his glorious riches in Christ Jesus.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Blessed the man who fears the LORD,
who greatly delights in his commands.
His posterity shall be mighty upon the earth;
the upright generation shall be blessed.
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
Well for the man who is gracious and lends,
who conducts his affairs with justice;
He shall never be moved;
the just one shall be in everlasting remembrance.
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.
His heart is steadfast; he shall not fear.
Lavishly he gives to the poor;
his generosity shall endure forever;
his horn shall be exalted in glory.
R. Blessed the man who fears the Lord.
or:
R. Alleluia.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to his disciples:
“I tell you, make friends for yourselves with dishonest wealth,
so that when it fails, you will be welcomed into eternal dwellings.
The person who is trustworthy in very small matters
is also trustworthy in great ones;
and the person who is dishonest in very small matters
is also dishonest in great ones.
If, therefore, you are not trustworthy with dishonest wealth,
who will trust you with true wealth?
If you are not trustworthy with what belongs to another,
who will give you what is yours?
No servant can serve two masters.
He will either hate one and love the other,
or be devoted to one and despise the other.
You cannot serve God and mammon.”The Pharisees, who loved money,
heard all these things and sneered at him.
And he said to them,
“You justify yourselves in the sight of others,
but God knows your hearts;
for what is of human esteem is an abomination in the sight of God.”

pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
